report.headline: Usage projected to climb from a below-average NBA role (15.3%, -0.97 sd) to an above-average EuroLeague share (22.9%, vs 20.6% league mean), but the true-shooting projection is not trustworthy for this transition.

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 22.9% in the EuroLeague, up from 15.3% in the source NBA season, placing the subject above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average usage of 20.6% (sd 4.4%).

risks.text: The true-shooting model loses to the trivial league-mean baseline (4.5% error vs 4.3%) on this metric, meaning the 62.5% projection should not be treated as informative despite its narrow-looking central value.

The subject's source usage rate stood at -0.97 standard deviations below the NBA average, notably lower than the -0.31 sd average standing of players who historically made this NBA-to-EuroLeague move, an atypical profile for this transition cohort.

The 80% interval for usage spans 18.5% to 27.2%, roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, so while the group-level shift is trustworthy, an individual outcome could land well below or above the point estimate.

strengths.text: Source-season true shooting of 64.7% sat 1.93 standard deviations above the NBA average that year, an elite efficiency mark.

The usage-rate model outperforms the best trivial baseline (3.2% mean absolute error vs 4.2% for league_mean over 277 held-out transitions), so the usage projection is grounded in a model that adds real signal.
The projected 22.9% usage rate places the subject above the EuroLeague average of 20.6%, consistent with a larger offensive role after the move.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 18.5% to 27.2%, and the 95% interval from 16.2% to 29.5% — a span of roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (sd 4.4%), enough to rank this player against peers but not to pin down a single number. For true shooting, the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.3%), so the 62.5% true-shooting projection and its interval (55.3%-69.8% at 80%, 51.5%-73.6% at 95%) carry no real information and should not be read as a forecast.
